dispute: Manner of Mohamed Oufkir's death, 16 August 1972

positions.moroccan: Official state account: suicide, following the collapse of the coup he had orchestrated.
positions.other: Family account (his daughter Malika Oufkir): multiple gunshot wounds — reported variously as three to the back and one to the neck, or wounds across several organs — inconsistent with self-infliction, implying execution by loyalist officers.

currentAssessment: Unresolved. No autopsy or forensic record has been consulted by this project. Distinguish the disagreement in fact (how many wounds, where) from the disagreement in interpretation (suicide vs execution).
whySourcesDisagree: The party that controlled the death scene and the official record — the Moroccan state — is also the party whose legitimacy the alternative account (execution by the regime) would undermine. This is not a French/Spanish/Moroccan colonial-era dispute; the usual three-tradition template doesn't apply cleanly to a post-1961 state-vs-family dispute, which is itself worth noting.

dispute: Zaian dead at El Herri, 13 November 1914

positions.moroccan: 182 (the 1991 HCAR/state monument repeats the French figure)

currentAssessment: A French floor, not an independently corroborated total. The monument is not independent corroboration.
whySourcesDisagree: Not a French-vs-Moroccan dispute in the usual sense — both traditions currently repeat the same uncorroborated number.

dispute: Who decided the 1953 deposition of Mohammed V

positions.french: El Glaoui and the notables took the initiative
positions.moroccan: Paris and the Résidence orchestrated it; El Glaoui's role was instrumental, not originating

currentAssessment: Settleable from Résidence–Paris correspondence, May–August 1953, not yet consulted.
whySourcesDisagree: Each tradition places responsibility with the actor least sympathetic to it.

positions.moroccan: Reported higher; no Moroccan primary count located yet by this workspace
positions.other: German 2,000–3,000 (embarrassing France served Berlin's interests during the 1905–1911 crisis period)

currentAssessment: Unresolvable on present evidence. State the range and the definitions; do not collapse to one figure.
whySourcesDisagree: No party to the bombardment had an incentive to count accurately: France to minimise a scandal, Germany to maximise one.

positions.french: Killed in a clash with French-allied partisans
positions.moroccan: Killed by his own son Hassan (most repeated); alternatively, in a clash with a party his sons had joined

currentAssessment: Disputed. Three different claims routinely collapsed into one. Treat the patricide narrative with particular caution.
whySourcesDisagree: The patricide version is narratively convenient in a way that should itself prompt scrutiny, not confidence.

positions.spanish: 7,875 / 8,180 / 8,668 / 13,363 — competing totals depending on whether Moroccan Regulares are counted

currentAssessment: Definitional, not merely evidentiary. State the range and the definitions.
whySourcesDisagree: The count depends on who is counted as Spanish — Spanish sources are, uniquely, unreliable on their own casualties.

positions.french: Oufkir named by a French court
positions.other: Dlimi, Mossad and CIA involvement alleged but not established

currentAssessment: Documents exist and are withheld. A different category from unknown.
whySourcesDisagree: This is not primarily a source-conflict; it is an access-conflict. Distinguish withheld from unknown, per standing rule 5.
